action: Organisations using Maileva: ask which of your recipients are affected and whether you must notify them or the regulator. People in France: be wary of letters, calls or messages that use your name and address to seem genuine.
exec: A breach at a mailing supplier exposed data that client organisations, including healthcare and housing bodies, had entrusted to it.
plain: A cyberattack on Maileva, a mail-services company owned by France's La Poste, exposed the names and postal addresses of 22 million people whose letters it handles for other organisations.
summary: A cyberattack on Maileva, La Poste's mail-services subsidiary, exposed first names, last names and postal addresses of 22 million people (next.ink: potentially exposed), mostly recipients of mail sent for client organisations. La Poste says the regulator CNIL was notified and a complaint filed; next.ink reports the Paris prosecutor opened an investigation. Maileva says bank details were not compromised. The attack dates from mid-September.
title: Breach at La Poste subsidiary Maileva exposes 22 million people in France

validation.note: Security Affairs, next.ink (16 Nov) and IT-Connect (16 Nov) each state the 22 million figure and the data types, citing La Poste's 15 Nov communique (not opened directly). next.ink relays the Paris prosecutor's confirmation to AFP of an investigation.

date_note: Reported November 15; Security Affairs says the attack itself dates from mid-September 2026.
